faultCodes.meaning: Warning: Loss of Communication - the module has not communicated with the master controller for longer than 5 minutes; the warning clears once communication is re-established
likelyCauses: Modbus/RS-485 wiring to the unit controller open, reversed polarity or unterminated
Master controller powered down or not polling this module
Stand-alone installation with no master controller (warning is informational)
checks: Confirm whether the unit uses the Modbus link at all; if not, ignore (no trip, no lockout)
Check the communication wiring polarity/continuity and the controller's Modbus address/baud settings (source: KB 1769)
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1769 'Green Flash Code 1 on CoreSense Module' (references AE8-1384) + Copeland KB 1818 'Alert/Lock Codes for CoreSense Diagnostics module for Air-conditioning Scroll Compressors' + AE8-1408 R3 / AE8-1384 (CoreSense Communications 13-15 t / 20-40 t) LED flash code table

faultCodes.meaning: Warning: Short Cycling
likelyCauses: Thermostat/controller cycling the compressor on and off rapidly
Pressure-switch (LPS/HPS) cycling
Low charge causing LPS trips
checks: Log run/off times; confirm minimum run and off timers in the controller
Check pressure switch operation and system charge
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1818 'Alert/Lock Codes for CoreSense Diagnostics module for Air-conditioning Scroll Compressors' + AE8-1408 R3 / AE8-1384 (CoreSense Communications 13-15 t / 20-40 t) LED flash code table

faultCodes.meaning: Warning: Open/Shorted Scroll Thermistor
likelyCauses: Discharge/scroll thermistor leads open or shorted at the module or Fusite
Failed scroll (discharge) thermistor
Wrong module for the compressor model
checks: Ohm the scroll thermistor circuit at the module terminals and compare with the resistance table in AE8-1408/AE8-1384 for the module version
Inspect the thermistor plug and wiring for chafing/moisture
Warning only - the compressor keeps running, but scroll high-temperature protection (Red 4) is lost until repaired
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1408 R3 'CoreSense Communications for 13 to 15 Ton Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED flash code table (Warning codes / Alert codes) / Copeland AE8-1384 R5/R9 'CoreSense Communications for 20 to 40 Ton Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - Table 6 LED flash code information (Code 4 - green Warning LED four times)

faultCodes.meaning: Alert: Motor High Temperature
likelyCauses: Motor overheating from low suction gas flow (low charge, restriction, low evaporator airflow)
High superheat / return-gas temperature
Low voltage or unbalanced 3-phase voltage
Failed contactor contact / single-phasing
checks: Measure suction superheat at the compressor
Measure line-to-line voltage under load and phase imbalance (< 2 %)
Compare running amps per phase to nameplate RLA
Check condenser fan and head pressure
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1818 'Alert/Lock Codes for CoreSense Diagnostics module for Air-conditioning Scroll Compressors' + AE8-1408 R3 / AE8-1384 (CoreSense Communications 13-15 t / 20-40 t) LED flash code table

faultCodes.meaning: Alert: Open/Shorted Motor Thermistor
likelyCauses: Thermistor leads open or shorted at the module or Fusite
Failed internal motor thermistor
Wrong compressor/module combination
checks: Ohm the thermistor circuit at the module terminals against the value in the Copeland bulletin for the module version
Inspect thermistor plug and wiring for damage
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1818 'Alert/Lock Codes for CoreSense Diagnostics module for Air-conditioning Scroll Compressors' + AE8-1408 R3 / AE8-1384 (CoreSense Communications 13-15 t / 20-40 t) LED flash code table

faultCodes.meaning: Alert: Short Cycling lockout - the module flashes the red Alert LED three times indicating the compressor is locked out due to short cycling; a Code 3 Alert opens the M2-M1 contacts
likelyCauses: Repeated short cycles beyond the module's threshold
Pressure-switch cycling, controller demand chatter
checks: Same as Green 3; find the cycling cause before resetting
Reset by cycling module power (or Modbus reset command) after the cause is corrected
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1768 'CoreSense Red Flash Code 3' + Copeland KB 1818 'Alert/Lock Codes for CoreSense Diagnostics module for Air-conditioning Scroll Compressors' + AE8-1408 R3 / AE8-1384 (CoreSense Communications 13-15 t / 20-40 t) LED flash code table

faultCodes.meaning: Alert: Scroll High Temperature lockout
likelyCauses: High discharge temperature: low charge, high compression ratio (dirty condenser, high head pressure), loss of condenser fan, high superheat
Low suction pressure operation
checks: Measure discharge line temperature 6 in. from the compressor (Copeland limit is 225 F)
Check condenser airflow/cleanliness and head pressure
Verify charge and superheat
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1818 'Alert/Lock Codes for CoreSense Diagnostics module for Air-conditioning Scroll Compressors' + AE8-1408 R3 / AE8-1384 (CoreSense Communications 13-15 t / 20-40 t) LED flash code table

faultCodes.meaning: Alert: Locked Rotor - when four consecutive Code 5 events are recorded, the module will lockout the compressor and flash red five times
likelyCauses: Compressor mechanically seized or starting against unequalized pressure
Single-phasing / phase problem at start (bulletin troubleshooting: check the contactor and the module phasing wires A-B-C)
Low voltage at the compressor terminals during start
checks: Measure all three line voltages at the contactor load side during a start attempt
Verify the module current/phasing leads A-B-C are routed through the correct compressor leads (field practice: a swapped sensing lead mimics a locked rotor)
Check LRA draw versus nameplate; allow pressure equalisation before restart
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1384 R5/R9 'CoreSense Communications for 20 to 40 Ton Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - Table 6 LED flash code information (Code 5 Locked Rotor; lockout after four consecutive events)

faultCodes.meaning: Alert: Missing Phase
likelyCauses: Open phase upstream (blown fuse, failed contactor pole, loose lug)
Utility single-phasing
checks: Measure all three line-to-line voltages at the contactor load side while calling for cooling
Inspect fuses, disconnect and contactor contacts
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1818 'Alert/Lock Codes for CoreSense Diagnostics module for Air-conditioning Scroll Compressors' + AE8-1408 R3 / AE8-1384 (CoreSense Communications 13-15 t / 20-40 t) LED flash code table

faultCodes.meaning: Alert: Reverse Phase - the module flashes the red Alert LED seven times indicating a reverse phase in two of the three leads to the compressor; a Code 7 Alert opens the M2-M1 contacts and the module locks out after one Code 7 Alert; a power cycle or Modbus reset command is required to clear the lockout
likelyCauses: Two line leads swapped at the disconnect, contactor or compressor terminals (new install, contactor/compressor replacement, utility work)
Scroll compressors are direction-sensitive - running reversed makes noise, does not pump, and overheats
checks: Verify phase sequence at the contactor load side with a phase-rotation meter; swap two line leads upstream of the module sensing point
Never swap leads between module and compressor if the module senses phase on its own inputs - correct rotation at the line side (field practice)
Reset: cycle power to the module after correcting rotation
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1408 R3 'CoreSense Communications for 13 to 15 Ton Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED flash code table (Warning codes / Alert codes) (Code 7 Reverse Phase, lockout after 1 Alert)

faultCodes.meaning: Reserved For Future Use (not assigned on the 13-40 ton CoreSense Communications module)
likelyCauses: Not a defined fault on this module - if a red 8 is seen, confirm which module/bulletin the unit actually has (on the single-phase AE8-1379 module and Comfort Alert, code 8 = Welded Contactor)
checks: Read the module part number and match it to the bulletin (KB 1819 / AE8-1408 / AE8-1384)
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1408 R3 'CoreSense Communications for 13 to 15 Ton Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED flash code table (Warning codes / Alert codes) (Code 8 Reserved For Future Use) / Copeland AE8-1384 R5/R9 'CoreSense Communications for 20 to 40 Ton Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - Table 6 LED flash code information (Code 8 Future Use, N/A)

faultCodes.meaning: Alert: Module Low Voltage - the module flashes the red Alert LED nine times indicating low module voltage on the T2-T1 terminals for more than 5 seconds; a Code 9 Alert opens the M2-M1 contacts; it resets after 5 minutes once voltage returns to the normal range
likelyCauses: Undersized or overloaded control transformer (low VA)
Blown fuse in the transformer secondary, loose T1/T2 wiring
Wrong module part number for the supply voltage
checks: Verify the module part number matches the control voltage (KB 1765)
Check the transformer VA rating against connected load and measure T1-T2 under load
Check for a blown fuse in the transformer secondary
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1765 'CoreSense Red Flash Code 9 for 20 to 40 Ton Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning' + Copeland AE8-1384 R5/R9 'CoreSense Communications for 20 to 40 Ton Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - Table 6 LED flash code information (Code 9 Module Low Voltage)

faultCodes.meaning: Code 1 - Long Run Time: the module flashes yellow one time when the compressor operates for longer than 18 continuous hours; alert only, the module will not lockout the compressor for this condition
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge
Evaporator/condenser airflow restriction (dirty filter/coil, blower or condenser fan problem)
Undersized or heavily loaded system / extreme heat load
Thermostat calling continuously or miswired
checks: Measure superheat/subcooling against the unit charging chart
Check filters, coils, blower and condenser fan
Confirm the thermostat demand actually drops out
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2086 'Yellow LED display in an Air Conditioning CoreSense Diagnostics module' + Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table

faultCodes.meaning: Code 2 - Compressor (Pressure) Trip: the module flashes yellow two times when the compressor operates from 12 seconds to 15 minutes followed by a trip condition lasting longer than 7 minutes
likelyCauses: High-pressure switch trip: dirty condenser, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables
Low-pressure switch trip: low charge, restriction, low airflow
Compressor internal overload opening on a hot compressor
checks: Check condenser fan operation first; compare head pressure with outdoor ambient
Read suction pressure / superheat for a low-charge or restriction trip
Check HPS/LPS settings and wiring
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2082 'Alarm Code 2 Yellow Flash 2 in the Air Conditioning CoreSense Diagnostics module' + Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table

faultCodes.meaning: Lock code 2 - Pressure trip lockout: when four consecutive or ten total Code 2 events are recorded, the module will lockout the compressor and flash red two times
likelyCauses: Repeated pressure-switch or overload trips (see Yellow 2)
checks: Correct the pressure/overload cause, then reset by cycling module power (disconnect the C terminal / 24 V) per KB 2070
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2082 + Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table

faultCodes.meaning: Code 3 - Pressure Switch Cycling (short cycling): the module flashes yellow three times when the compressor operates from 12 seconds to 15 minutes followed by a trip condition lasting between 35 seconds and 7 minutes
likelyCauses: Low-pressure switch cycling on low charge or a restriction
High-pressure switch cycling (condenser fan intermittent, dirty coil)
Thermostat chatter or loose Y wiring
checks: Watch suction/head pressure through a cycle to see which switch opens
Verify the Y demand is steady (24 V at the module)
Check charge, airflow and condenser fan
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2078 'Yellow flash 3 in the Air Conditioning CoreSense Diagnostics module' (reproduces AE8-1379 R2 table row)

faultCodes.meaning: Lock code 3 - Short-cycling lockout: when four consecutive or ten total Code 3 events are recorded, the module will lockout the compressor and flash red three times
likelyCauses: Repeated pressure-switch cycling (see Yellow 3)
checks: Find and fix the cycling cause before resetting; reset by cycling module power per KB 2070
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2078 'Yellow flash 3 in the Air Conditioning CoreSense Diagnostics module' (reproduces AE8-1379 R2 table row)

faultCodes.meaning: Code 4 - Locked Rotor Trip: the module flashes yellow four times when the compressor trips within 12 seconds of operation and does not reset and start within 35 seconds
likelyCauses: Compressor mechanically seized or starting against unequalized pressure
Failed run capacitor / start components (single-phase)
Low voltage at the compressor terminals during start
Miswired module current sensor (false locked rotor)
checks: Measure voltage at the compressor terminals during a start attempt
Test the run capacitor (uF) and start relay/capacitor if fitted
Confirm LRA draw followed by immediate overload trip; allow pressure equalisation time
Verify the compressor common lead passes through the module current sensor
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2079 'Yellow flash 4 in the Air Conditioning CoreSense Diagnostics module' (reproduces AE8-1379 R2 table row)

faultCodes.meaning: Lock code 4 - Locked rotor lockout: when ten consecutive Code 4 events are recorded, the module will lockout the compressor and flash red four times
likelyCauses: Repeated locked-rotor starts (see Yellow 4)
checks: Do not keep resetting - each attempt heats the windings; diagnose start components/voltage, then reset per KB 2070
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2079 'Yellow flash 4 in the Air Conditioning CoreSense Diagnostics module' (reproduces AE8-1379 R2 table row)

faultCodes.meaning: Code 5 - Compressor (Moderate Run) Trip: the module flashes yellow five times when the compressor has operated between 15 minutes and 18 hours, followed by a compressor trip lasting longer than 7 minutes
likelyCauses: Internal overload opening after a long run (hot compressor: low charge / high superheat, high head pressure, low voltage)
Pressure switch opening after a long run
Open contactor/fuse or wiring to the compressor while Y is still present
checks: Check for 24 V at Y with no compressor current during the trip
Measure discharge temperature, superheat and head pressure before the trip recurs
Ohm C-S-R windings after the compressor cools; inspect contactor and wiring
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1817 'CoreSense Diagnostics Module for Air-conditioning Scroll Compressors and System Protection' + Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table

faultCodes.meaning: Lock code 5 - Moderate-run trip lockout: when four consecutive Code 5 events occur, the module locks out and flashes red five times
likelyCauses: Repeated overload/pressure trips after long runs (see Yellow 5)
checks: Correct the cause, then reset per KB 2070
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 1817 + Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table

faultCodes.meaning: Code 6 - Open Start Circuit: the module will lockout the compressor and flash red six times if it detects a demand signal on the Y terminal and current in the R (run) winding of the compressor, but no current in the S (start) winding for 2 seconds
likelyCauses: Open start winding
Failed start capacitor / start relay, open start-circuit wiring or terminal
Module S-lead current sensor not installed around the start lead
checks: Ohm C-S and compare with C-R (start winding resistance is normally higher than run)
Check the start capacitor and potential relay if fitted
Verify module current-sensing lead routing before condemning the compressor (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2075 'Red flash 6 in the Air Conditioning CoreSense Diagnostics module' (reproduces AE8-1379 R2 table row)

faultCodes.meaning: Code 7 - Open Run Circuit: the module has detected Y or Y1 and current in the S winding of the compressor and no current in the R winding for 2 seconds
likelyCauses: Open run winding
Failed run capacitor or open run-circuit wiring/terminal
Module R-lead current sensor not around the run lead
checks: Ohm C-R
Test the run capacitor (uF) and its wiring
Verify module current-sensing lead routing
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table (Code 7, as summarised in Copeland KB series 2072-2086)

faultCodes.meaning: Code 8 - Welded Contactor: the module has detected line currents in the R and S windings while Y or Y1 is at 0 VAC for 15 seconds
likelyCauses: Contactor contacts welded closed - compressor runs with no thermostat demand
Contactor miswired / bypassed so the compressor is fed without Y
checks: Confirm compressor current with Y de-energised
Replace the contactor; check for the cause of welding (low voltage coil, high inrush, pitted contacts)
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table (Code 8, as summarised in Copeland KB series 2072-2086)

faultCodes.meaning: Code 9 - Module Low Voltage supply: the module flashes yellow nine times if the module supply voltage drops below 17 VAC for 2 seconds
likelyCauses: Undersized/overloaded 24 V transformer
Low line voltage, loose common/R wiring to the module
Excess load on the control circuit (accessory relays, long thermostat runs)
checks: Measure 24 V at the module under load with the contactor pulled in
Check transformer VA rating and secondary fuse/breaker
Check line voltage at the transformer primary
faultCodes.source: Copeland KB 2072 'Yellow flash 9 in the Air Conditioning CoreSense Diagnostics module' (reproduces AE8-1379 R2 table row)

faultCodes.meaning: Code 9 - Over-Current Protection: when the current at the PROT terminal is greater than 2 A for 40 ms the module flashes a Code 9; the red LED flashes 9 times with the yellow LED remaining off - the module is mis-wired or the contactor coil is shorted to ground (Code 9 is not printed on the module label)
likelyCauses: PROT output miswired (e.g. PROT tied to common or to the wrong contactor coil terminal)
Contactor coil shorted to ground / failed coil
checks: Ohm the contactor coil to ground and coil resistance
Re-check the module wiring against the diagram in AE8-1379 (PROT in series with the contactor coil)
On the UltraTech (AE8-1385) two-stage module the same fault is Code 10
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table (Code 9 Over-Current Protection); same function is Code 10 in AE8-1385 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll UltraTech Air Conditioning Compressors'

faultCodes.meaning: TRIP: the module detects the presence of a demand signal from the thermostat, however no current to the compressor is detected by the module - typically the compressor protector is open, or supply power to the compressor is missing
likelyCauses: Internal overload open (hot compressor)
Open contactor, blown fuse, tripped breaker or open wiring to the compressor
Open winding
checks: Check line voltage at the contactor load side with Y present
Let the compressor cool and ohm C-S-R
Inspect the contactor coil and contacts
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1379 R2 (Feb 2015) 'CoreSense Diagnostics for Copeland Scroll Air Conditioning Compressors' - LED Troubleshooting Information table (Module LED description: red TRIP LED)

faultCodes.meaning: Long Run Time - Compressor is running extremely long run cycles
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge
Evaporator/condenser airflow restriction
Undersized or heavily loaded system
Thermostat calling continuously
checks: Measure superheat/subcooling against the charging chart
Check filters, coils, blower and condenser fan
On commercial modules with a solenoid output: if Code 1 or 9 appears while running, the module de-energises the unloader solenoid and the compressor continues at part load
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107)

faultCodes.meaning: System Pressure Trip - Discharge or suction pressure out of limits or compressor overloaded
likelyCauses: HPS trip: dirty condenser, fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables
LPS trip: low charge, restriction, low airflow
Internal overload opening
checks: Read head and suction pressure at the trip
Check HPS/LPS settings and condenser fan
Commercial 3-phase module: lockout = yes
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107)

faultCodes.meaning: Short Cycling - Compressor is running only briefly
likelyCauses: Pressure switch cycling
Thermostat chatter or loose Y wiring
Low charge
checks: Verify steady Y demand
Check LPS/HPS cycling and charge
Commercial 3-phase module: lockout = yes
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107)

faultCodes.meaning: Locked Rotor
likelyCauses: Compressor seized or starting against unequalized pressure
Failed run/start capacitor or relay
Low voltage at the compressor terminals
checks: Measure start voltage at the compressor terminals
Test capacitors (uF)
Confirm LRA then immediate overload trip; allow equalisation
Commercial 3-phase module: lockout = yes
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107)

faultCodes.meaning: Open Circuit
likelyCauses: Internal overload open (hot compressor)
Open contactor, fuse or wiring to the compressor
Open winding
checks: 24 V at Y with no compressor current
Ohm C-S-R after cool-down
Inspect contactor and wiring
Commercial 3-phase module: lockout = no
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107)

faultCodes.meaning: Open Start Circuit - Current only in run circuit (single-phase modules). On the commercial 3-phase Comfort Alert module code 6 = Missing Phase (lockout = yes)
likelyCauses: Single-phase: open start winding, failed start capacitor/relay, open start wiring
3-phase: open phase upstream (fuse, contactor pole, loose lug)
checks: Single-phase: ohm C-S vs C-R; test start components
3-phase: measure all three line-to-line voltages at the contactor load side
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107) / Copeland 'Comfort Alert diagnostics for commercial applications' brochure (943-0033-00) and User's Manual 2005ECT-191 R6 (543-0038-01/-02, 543-0071-00) - diagnostic code / lockout table

faultCodes.meaning: Open Run Circuit - Current only in start circuit (single-phase modules). On the commercial 3-phase Comfort Alert module code 7 = Reverse Phase (lockout = yes)
likelyCauses: Single-phase: open run winding, failed run capacitor, open run wiring
3-phase: two line leads swapped
checks: Single-phase: ohm C-R; test run capacitor
3-phase: check phase rotation with a phase-sequence meter and swap two line leads at the line side
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107) / Copeland 'Comfort Alert diagnostics for commercial applications' brochure (943-0033-00) and User's Manual 2005ECT-191 R6 (543-0038-01/-02, 543-0071-00) - diagnostic code / lockout table

faultCodes.meaning: Welded Contactor - Compressor always runs
likelyCauses: Contactor contacts welded closed
Contactor miswired or bypassed
checks: Compressor current with Y de-energised
Replace the contactor
Commercial 3-phase module: lockout = no
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107)

faultCodes.meaning: Low Voltage - Control circuit < 17 VAC
likelyCauses: Undersized/overloaded 24 V transformer
Low line voltage, loose control wiring
checks: Measure 24 V at the module with the contactor energised
Check transformer VA and line voltage
If TRIP and ALERT LEDs flash at the same time, control-circuit voltage is too low for the module to operate
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107)

faultCodes.meaning: TRIP: there is a demand signal from the thermostat but no current to the compressor is detected by Comfort Alert - typically the compressor protector is open, or supply power to the compressor is missing
likelyCauses: Internal overload open
Open contactor/fuse/breaker or wiring
Open winding
checks: Check line voltage at the contactor load side with Y present
Ohm C-S-R after cool-down
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107) - LED description

faultCodes.code: Comfort Alert TRIP and ALERT LEDs flashing together
faultCodes.meaning: Control circuit voltage is too low for operation
likelyCauses: 24 V control voltage below the module's operating minimum
checks: Measure control voltage at the module; check the transformer and line voltage
faultCodes.source: Copeland/Emerson Comfort Alert Diagnostics User's Manual 543-0032-00 / 543-0033-00 / 543-0038-00 - 'Flash Code' table (also reproduced in ICP N4H3 installation instructions p.19 and Rheem RRNL IOM p.107) - LED description

faultCodes.meaning: Alert (warning) condition on the CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11 module - the compressor keeps running
likelyCauses: Oil-pressure warning (differential below 7-9 psid / 0.48-0.62 bar for 4 s, before the 120 s lockout)
Other warning-level condition shown as text on the LCD
checks: Read the LCD alarm text and the last-ten alarm history (alarm 1 = most recent)
Check oil level, oil pressure differential and suction-line oil return
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1368 R2/R3 'CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11 for Copeland Discus Compressors' - LED status description

faultCodes.meaning: Control module has failed (steady red = module failure, not a compressor fault code)
likelyCauses: Failed CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11 module or its power supply
See Copeland KB 2411 'Solid Red LED on CoreSense Diagnostics V2.11' and KB 4655 'FAILSAFE mode' before replacing
checks: Check module supply voltage and wiring
Follow KB 2411 / KB 4655 (FAILSAFE mode reset) before condemning the module
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1368 R2/R3 'CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11 for Copeland Discus Compressors' - LED status description + Copeland KB 2411 / KB 4655

faultCodes.meaning: Low oil pressure lockout: once the oil pressure differential falls below 0.48-0.62 bar (7-9 psid) for 2 minutes (120 s) the module shuts the compressor off and a 'low oil pressure lockout' is reported; a warning is issued after 4 seconds below the threshold
likelyCauses: Low oil level / oil not returning (suction-line sizing, traps, long off-cycles)
Refrigerant flooding/dilution of the oil
Oil pump or oil-pressure sensor problem
checks: Check crankcase oil level and oil-pressure differential
Check suction superheat and oil return; look for floodback
Manual reset required at the compressor (KB 4658 'Reset a lockout on CoreSense Diagnostics V2.11' / reset button under the module)
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1368 R2/R3 'CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11 for Copeland Discus Compressors' - LED status description - Insufficient oil pressure protection

faultCodes.meaning: Discharge temperature protection: an NTC sensor in the cylinder head (factory-installed) shuts the compressor off if discharge temperature exceeds 154 C (310 F) until it cools to an acceptable level
likelyCauses: High compression ratio: dirty condenser, condenser fan failure, high head pressure
High superheat / low suction pressure, low charge
Defective sensor or wiring
checks: Measure discharge line temperature and head pressure
Check superheat, charge and condenser airflow
Ohm the NTC head sensor if the trip does not match measured temperature
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1368 R2/R3 'CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11 for Copeland Discus Compressors' - LED status description - High discharge temperature protection

faultCodes.meaning: Locked rotor detection with trip and lockout alarms: 10 consecutive trip alarms result in a lockout alarm requiring manual reset
likelyCauses: Mechanically seized compressor or start against unequalized pressure
Phase loss / low voltage at start
checks: Measure line voltages during start, check phase presence
Check LRA and equalisation; manual reset after the cause is fixed
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1368 R2/R3 'CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11 for Copeland Discus Compressors' - LED status description - Locked rotor protection

faultCodes.meaning: Phase loss protection: if any phase voltage is less than 84 % of the maximum for 1 second the module trips; trip time is 5 minutes with automatic reset
likelyCauses: Open phase upstream (fuse, contactor pole, loose lug)
Severe voltage imbalance
checks: Measure all three line-to-line voltages at the contactor load side
Inspect fuses, disconnect and contactor
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1368 R2/R3 'CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11 for Copeland Discus Compressors' - LED status description - Phase loss protection

ledPatterns.pattern: 3-phase CoreSense Communications module (AE8-1408 13-15 t / AE8-1384 20-40 t): solid green
3-phase module: green flashing N times, pause, repeat
ledPatterns.meaning: Warning code N - no trip, no lockout (1 loss of communication, 3 short cycling, 4 open/shorted scroll thermistor)
checks: Count flashes between pauses

ledPatterns.pattern: 3-phase module: red flashing N times, pause, repeat
ledPatterns.meaning: Alert code N - compressor tripped via the M1-M2 contacts and possibly locked out
checks: Codes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 lock out; 6 and 9 auto-reset when the condition clears; 8 reserved

ledPatterns.pattern: 3-phase module: red flash N times, pause, solid red, pause, repeat
ledPatterns.meaning: Lockout condition (AE8-1408 R3: 'a lockout condition produces a red flash, followed by a pause, a solid red, a second pause, and then repeated')
checks: Correct the cause, then cycle module power or send the Modbus reset command

ledPatterns.pattern: AE8-1379 single-phase/light-commercial module (571-0066-00 AC / 571-0067-00 HP): solid yellow
ledPatterns.meaning: Module powered and compressor/system running normally

ledPatterns.pattern: AE8-1379 module: yellow ALERT LED flashes N times, pause, repeat
ledPatterns.meaning: ALERT code N - abnormal system condition (1 long run, 2 pressure trip, 3 pressure-switch cycling, 4 locked rotor trip, 5 moderate-run trip, 9 low module voltage)
checks: Count consecutive flashes; the code repeats until cleared

ledPatterns.meaning: TRIP - thermostat demand present but no compressor current detected (protector open or no supply power)

ledPatterns.pattern: AE8-1379 module: red TRIP/LOCK LED flashes N times, pause, repeat
ledPatterns.meaning: LOCK code N - compressor lockout active (2, 3, 4, 5 after repeated alerts; 6 open start circuit; 7 open run circuit; 8 welded contactor; 9 with yellow off = over-current on PROT)
checks: Reset by cycling module power (disconnect the C terminal) per KB 2070 after the cause is fixed

ledPatterns.pattern: Comfort Alert module: green POWER LED on
ledPatterns.meaning: Module has power; supply voltage present at the module terminals

ledPatterns.pattern: Comfort Alert module: red TRIP LED on
ledPatterns.meaning: Demand signal from the thermostat but no current to the compressor detected (protector open or missing supply power)

ledPatterns.pattern: Comfort Alert module: yellow ALERT LED flashes N times, pause, repeat
ledPatterns.meaning: ALERT flash code N (see 'Comfort Alert code N'); on power-up the last ALERT code before shutdown is displayed for one minute
checks: Reset by removing 24 VAC from the module (cycle power)

ledPatterns.pattern: Comfort Alert module: TRIP and ALERT flashing at the same time
ledPatterns.meaning: Control circuit voltage too low for operation

ledPatterns.pattern: Discus CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11: steady green / flashing green / flashing orange (yellow) / flashing red / steady red
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal, no fault / alert (warning) / compressor tripped, auto-reset / lockout (manual reset) / control module failed
checks: Read the fault text on the 2-line LCD; last ten alarms are stored, alarm 1 = most recent

diagnosticTips: Identify the module first (KB 1819 / KB 1816): 571-0066-00 (service 971-0066-00) is the two-wire AC module and 571-0067-00 (971-0067-00) the three-wire heat-pump module covered by AE8-1379 (yellow ALERT / red TRIP-LOCK LEDs, current-sensing on R and S leads, installed in the unit electrical panel near the contactor). The 13-15 ton (AE8-1408) and 20-40 ton (AE8-1384) CoreSense Communications modules mount in the compressor terminal box, sense motor and scroll thermistors plus 3-phase supply, and use a green WARNING / red ALERT scheme with M1-M2 pilot-duty contacts and Modbus. Comfort Alert (543-/943-0032, -0033, -0038) is the older current-sensing module with green POWER, red TRIP and yellow ALERT LEDs. The same flash count means different things on each - always read the code against the right table.
Reading a code: count the consecutive flashes between pauses; the code repeats until cleared. On AE8-1408/1384 modules a lockout is shown as red flashes, pause, solid red, pause, repeat.

Reset (AE8-1379 module, KB 2070): cycle power to the module by disengaging the COMMON (C) terminal. This clears the present ALERT or TRIP/LOCK and allows normal operation but does not clear the seven-day operating history stored in the module. Fix the cause first - a locked-out compressor is protecting itself.

Reset (13-40 ton CoreSense Communications): cycle module power (T1-T2) or send the Modbus reset command; alerts 6 (missing phase) and 9 (module low voltage) clear automatically once the condition is normal (code 9 after 5 minutes).
Reset (Comfort Alert): remove 24 VAC from the module. On every power-up the module displays the last ALERT code for one minute - use this to read a code the customer saw earlier.
Reset (Discus CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11): reset button below the control module, or per KB 4658; a FAILSAFE-mode module is reset per KB 4655. Lockouts require a manual reset at the compressor.

Current-sensing modules (AE8-1379, Comfort Alert) infer faults from compressor current versus Y demand: a common/run/start lead that does not pass through the module's sensor gives false open-circuit, locked-rotor or welded-contactor codes - verify the sensing-lead routing (KB 1809 installation guidelines) before condemning a compressor.

Module history: AE8-1379 and AE8-1385 modules store a seven-day operating history that can be downloaded with the CoreSense PC Communication Software (see the AE bulletin 'Module History Download' section).
notes: Existing pack codes 'Green 1/3' and 'Red 1/2/3/4/6' are kept with the same code strings and meanings; this sidecar attributes them additionally to AE8-1408 R3 / AE8-1384, which is where the green-warning / red-alert scheme with motor and scroll thermistors is documented. KB 1818's title says 'CoreSense Diagnostics module', so the existing entry's naming is left as-is; verifiers should confirm KB 1818's body matches this scheme.
AE8-1379 module codes are labelled '(AE 1379 module)' because the flash count collides with the 3-phase scheme (e.g. red 6 = Missing Phase on AE8-1408/1384 but Open Start Circuit on AE8-1379).

Comfort Alert codes are labelled 'Comfort Alert code N'; code 6/7 differ between the residential single-phase modules (open start / open run circuit) and the commercial 3-phase module (missing phase / reverse phase) - both meanings are given in the same entry.
AE8-1385 (UltraTech two-stage) uses the same yellow/red code set as AE8-1379 except that Over-Current Protection is Code 10 instead of Code 9; its full table was not transcribed.

Discus: only the LED colour states and the protection descriptions from AE8-1368 were seen; the numbered flash-code tables (AE8-1367 R6/R8 Tables 3-5 for CoreSense Protection, AE8-1368 'Module operation-code description' for CoreSense Diagnostics v2.11) were not surfaced by search and are NOT transcribed. Refrigeration-scroll CoreSense Diagnostics (AE8-1424 / AE4-1383 K5 Table 7) are outside this platform id and live under 'coresense-diagnostics-k5-3ph'.
The AE8-1384 20-40 ton table may also define a green Warning code 2; it was not seen and is omitted.
